To continue building your position and setting up winning lines while maintaining pressure against O's current placements, dropping a piece to strengthen the central control is a solid approach. Let's look at dropping into column C to add to the existing pieces or taking a foundational spot in row 2. 

Dropping at C1 adds a piece to the bottom of the C1 shaft, which currently has no pieces and will sit at L1, helping build a vertical or diagonal line potential.

MOVE: drop C1

To counter O's horizontal pressure in row 3 (O currently has O3, B3, C3, D3 in layer 1, and O at C3 in layer 2), we can establish our own strong line or drop strategically. Let's look at adding to our own pieces or disrupting. Dropping at C1 gives us a nice vertical or diagonal potential, but let's check shaft B2 or B3. 

Wait, looking at the board, O is threatening a lot on row 3 (B3, C3, D3 on L1). Let's drop into B3 to block or secure our own positioning.

MOVE: drop B3
